- **ep**: Epstein was a JPMorgan client from 1998 until 2013 — retained through his 2006 arrest and his 2008 guilty plea, for five more years. In June 2023 the bank agreed to pay approximately $290 million to settle a class action brought by more than a hundred victims, on the same day a federal judge granted the case class-action status. The settlement followed months of disclosures that the bank had ignored internal warnings and overlooked red flags because he was a valuable client. JPMorgan did not admit wrongdoing. It separately sought to recover over $80 million from its own former executive Jes Staley, arguing he should bear any civil liability — an institution suing its own former banker to shift responsibility for a relationship the institution maintained.

- **ep_ALLEGATIONS_REGISTER_v1.md**: ## What the government had, and didn't use - The **SDNY memo of December 2019** interviewed more than two dozen alleged victims and potential subjects. - It described Epstein working "with others, including employees and associates", who helped by "contacting victims and scheduling their sexual encounters with Epstein". - It weighed Maxwell, Lesley Groff (who denies wrongdoing), Brunel, Black and Staley, plus other names from finance, fashion and Hollywood that remain unidentified. - Its legal analysis is **almost entirely redacted**. - **Only Maxwell was charged.** - DOJ's position, from Blanche: "if we had information… about men who abused women, we would prosecute them." - The register sets that sentence beside the memo, and leaves the reader to weigh the two.
